exposure: Robson Classification groups (e.g., nulliparous women, women with previous caesarean, preterm pregnancies)
outcome: caesarean section rates for each Robson group
absolute and relative contributions of each group to the overall rate
cohort: The study included 9723 deliveries in a tertiary maternity hospital in southeastern Brazil between 2016 and 2020.
finding: The overall caesarean section rate was 38.9%, with Group 5 (women with a previous caesarean section) being the largest contributor, accounting for 37.1% of all caesarean sections.
mod_finding: Specific strategies, such as protocols to encourage vaginal birth after caesarean (VBAC) and improvements in induction management, were suggested to help reduce unnecessary caesarean interventions.
cross-section timing: Data was collected retrospectively from 2016 to 2020.
gest_age: Preterm pregnancies (Group 10) were a specific category studied, showing a caesarean rate of 50.7%.
